data.claim: Will Saturday's protests in France draw less than half last week's crowd?

current.title: Street unrest in France and Italy

data.resolution_source: French Interior Ministry national count of demonstrators for Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, as published by the ministry or relayed from it by AFP, Le Monde or franceinfo
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the Interior Ministry's nationwide count of protesters in France for Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, is below 275,000, which is half its count of 550,000 for Oct. 17. No if it is 275,000 or more. Use the latest full-day national figure the ministry publishes by 23:59 Paris time on Oct. 31, 2026; if it publishes only an intraday figure, use the latest one published by then. Ignore later revisions and any count by unions, organizers or independent counters. If the ministry publishes a national figure for Oct. 24, that figure settles the question whatever else happens. If it publishes none by the deadline: void if the national protest day was moved from Oct. 24 to a later date; otherwise Yes, including when the calls are withdrawn or banned or the protests are too scattered for a national count.

history.why: Unions stay out, curfews deter marchers, and second days usually shrink.

data.note: The Interior Ministry's full-day national count for Saturday, Oct. 24, published that evening, was 410,000. That is above the 275,000 threshold, which is half of the 550,000 counted on Oct. 17. The rule says the ministry's figure settles the question and later revisions are ignored. The only earlier ministry figure was an intraday count of about 35,000 at 13:00, which the full-day figure replaces.

evidence.quote: De nombreux manifestants, 410.000 selon le ministère de l'Intérieur, 800.000 selon la CGT, ont défilé ce samedi pour l'acte II de la mobilisation contre la vie chère.
evidence.title: Mobilisation du 24 octobre : 410.000 manifestants en France selon le gouvernement, 800.000 d'après la CGT

data.reasoning: Half of the Interior Ministry's Oct. 17 count of 550,000 is 275,000, and only the ministry's national count decides the question. The five main unions do not back Oct. 24 and keep their strength for the Nov. 5 strike. Local curfews, powers for prefects to ban gatherings, about 2,400 arrests and the treatment of the violence as organized crime make marching riskier for ordinary people. In 2018, the ministry counted about 282,000 Yellow Vests on the first Saturday and about 106,000 on the second. The ministry's count also runs below union counts. If the government bans the marches or the ministry publishes no national count, the result counts as less than half. Against this, Oct. 17 drew about three times the official estimate, the grievances on schools, diesel and the budget remain, and calls for Oct. 24 cover about 205 places.
data.uncertainty: Oct. 17 surprised the state by a factor of about three, so estimates of crowds from an open online call are weak.
data.rises_if: Prefects ban marches in large cities, the government declares a state of emergency, or new violence keeps families at home.
data.falls_if: Unions or student groups call their members to join Oct. 24, a new incident angers the public, or the number of planned protest sites grows sharply.

data.claim: Will Moody's keep France's credit rating where it is on Friday?

current.title: Street unrest in France and Italy

data.resolution_source: Moody's Ratings announcement on France at moodys.com, cross-checked with the Agence France Trésor's France credit ratings page and wire reports (Reuters, AFP).
data.resolution_rule: Yes if Moody's leaves France's long-term issuer rating at Aa3 in every announcement on France published by the end of Oct. 24, 2026 UTC, whatever it does to the outlook or review status, including when it publishes no rating action on France at its scheduled Oct. 23, 2026 review. No if, by the end of Oct. 24, 2026 UTC, Moody's announces any change to that rating, such as a cut to A1 or below, even if the change is later reversed. Void only if, by the end of Oct. 24, 2026 UTC, Moody's formally announces that it has moved the Oct. 23 review past Oct. 24, 2026 and has not changed the rating.

history.why: Moody's test is the December budget, which the riots do not settle by Friday.

data.note: Moody's finished its scheduled Oct. 23 periodic review of France without a formal rating action. The rating stayed at Aa3 and the outlook stayed negative. CNBC, Fortune and Seoul Economic Daily report the same thing. None of the reports found says Moody's changed the rating by the end of Oct. 24 UTC. The time is approximate: Fortune says the announcement came late Friday, and Seoul Economic Daily

evidence.quote: Moody's said it had concluded a periodic review of its rating, leaving it at Aa3, which has carried a negative outlook since last October.
evidence.title: France spared Moody's ratings downgrade as it struggles with unrest

data.reasoning: Moody's ties its negative outlook to whether France's institutions can make policy with a split parliament. The 2027 budget answers that in December, by a vote, by forced passage or by ordinance, and it has not failed yet. Moody's cut France in December 2024 only after a government fell over its budget, and in October 2025 it only turned its outlook negative while S&P cut early. Rating agencies usually count street violence only if it changes the budget or brings down a government. A warning, a negative outlook or a review for downgrade would all leave France at Aa3.
data.uncertainty: The negative outlook is a year old, inside the 12 to 18 months in which Moody's usually settles outlooks. The deficit is now expected near 5.4%, above the 5.0% that Moody's cited in April. The Moody's comment of Oct. 2 was stern, and a cut would only match Fitch and S&P. The riots raised borrowing costs and weakened a minority government that faces the Nov. 5 strike and a no-confidence motion.
data.rises_if: The week passes without new riots, the budget debate moves forward, or France's borrowing costs fall back before Friday.
data.falls_if: New riots break out, a no-confidence motion gains support, the government signals a budget failure, or France's 10-year borrowing cost climbs back toward 5% before Friday.
chain: The Oct. 17 riots added political risk, and France's 10-year borrowing cost rose about 7 basis points on Oct. 19.
Investors read that as raising the odds that Moody's cuts France's Aa3 grade at its review on Friday, Oct. 23.
Moody's said on Oct. 2 that its test is whether France's institutions can still make policy with a split parliament, with the 2027 budget's approval the open question.
That budget is settled in December, and the riots do not decide it by Friday.
Moody's held through the government collapse of October 2025 and cut in December 2024 only after a government fell over its budget.
Will Moody's keep France's credit rating where it is on Friday?

theses.claim: France will get through the riots without losing a credit grade this autumn: Moody's will keep France at Aa3 on Oct. 23 and wait for the 2027 budget's fate in December, and S&P will hold France at A+ at its Nov. 27 review.
theses.missed_link: Coverage treats the riots as one more push toward a downgrade on Friday. But Moody's has named its test: whether France's institutions can pass a budget and make policy with a split parliament. That answer comes in December, and Moody's has acted on France only after a concrete budget failure, holding through the October 2025 government collapse that drove S&P to cut early.
theses.moves: What the French state pays to borrow, and through it home-loan and business-loan rates in France; and the ratings of French banks and state-linked borrowers, which Moody's tends to cut after the state, as it did to several French banks within a week of the December 2024 downgrade.
theses.wrong_if: Moody's cuts France to A1 or lower on Oct. 23, or Moody's cites the unrest as a reason for acting, or Moody's or S&P cuts France before the 2027 budget's fate is settled.

data.claim: Will Indonesia's central bank hold off raising interest rates on Wednesday?
data.resolution_source: Bank Indonesia's press release on the result of its Board of Governors meeting ending Oct. 21, 2026, published at bi.go.id
data.resolution_rule: NO if Bank Indonesia announces an increase in the BI-Rate at any meeting, scheduled or unscheduled, between Oct. 17 and Oct. 21, 2026, even if it is later reversed. Otherwise YES if the BI-Rate announced after the Board of Governors meeting ending Oct. 21, 2026 is 5.75% or lower. Changes to the deposit or lending facility rates alone do not count. If the scheduled decision is not published by Oct. 21, 2026 and no increase has been announced in the meantime, the question is void.

history.why: Forced index selling is months away, and the rupiah fell under 1%.

data.note: The Board of Governors meeting on Oct 20-21, 2026 kept the BI-Rate at 5.75%, which meets the rule's 5.75%-or-lower condition. No BI-Rate increase was announced between Oct 17 and Oct 21. BI raised the Deposit Facility rate 25bp to 5.00% and held the Lending Facility rate at 6.50%, but the rule excludes facility-rate changes alone. Databoks (databoks.katadata.co.id, 21/10/2026 18:40 WIB) confirms t

evidence.quote: Bank Indonesia (BI) unexpectedly maintained its key interest rate at 5.75% for the fourth straight meeting on October 21
evidence.title: Indonesia Unexpectedly Holds Rates, Hikes DFR, Cuts RRR

data.reasoning: MSCI's proposal is a consultation, with a decision by June 30, 2027, so any forced index selling is months away. The rupiah fell less than 1% while the Jakarta Composite fell 11.57%, and Bank Indonesia already intervenes in the spot and forward markets and buys government bonds. It held in July, against most forecasts and with a weaker rupiah, and it held after MSCI's first warning earlier in 2026. Its new governor puts growth and coordination with the government beside stability.
data.uncertainty: Inflation of 3.28% sits near the top of the target band, the current-account deficit hit a record, and expectations of a U.S. rate rise in December add pressure. The rupiah sits near about 18,100 per dollar, the level that reportedly came before the bank's rise in June. Citigroup and OCBC now expect a rise, and the bank raised its rate a full point in May and June when the rupiah slid.
data.rises_if: The rupiah stays stronger than 18,100 per dollar, foreign selling of government bonds slows, or bank officials say interventions are enough.
data.falls_if: The rupiah weakens past 18,100 per dollar, foreign funds sell Indonesian government bonds fast, or U.S. yields jump before Oct. 21.
chain: On Oct. 15, MSCI proposed moving Indonesia out of its emerging-markets index.
Jakarta stocks fell 11.6% the next day, but the rupiah slipped less than 1% as Bank Indonesia sold dollars and bought bonds.
Citigroup and OCBC now see a rate rise at Bank Indonesia's Oct. 21 meeting.
The selling MSCI's move would force is in stocks, comes only if MSCI decides by June 2027, and a higher rate cannot fix free floats.
In July, with the rupiah weaker than now and most forecasters expecting a rise, Bank Indonesia held and used other tools.
Will Indonesia's central bank hold off raising interest rates on Wednesday?

theses.claim: Indonesia's MSCI scare will stay a stock-market problem. Bank Indonesia will defend the rupiah with interventions and bond buying rather than raise its 5.75% rate, holding it at its October and November meetings, so Indonesian borrowing costs do not rise because of MSCI.
theses.missed_link: Coverage treats the worst day for Jakarta stocks since 1998 as a currency emergency that forces a rate rise. But the selling MSCI's proposal would force is a one-time shift of roughly $3 billion to $7 billion out of stocks, it happens only if MSCI decides to go ahead by June 2027, and a higher interest rate does nothing about the free-float and ownership problems MSCI cited. The rupiah moved less than 1% while stocks fell 11.6%. In July, with the rupiah weaker than now and most forecasters calling for a rise, Bank Indonesia held and used other tools. Its new governor has put growth and coordination with the government beside stability.
theses.moves: Indonesian bank loan and mortgage rates, the government's borrowing costs, bank lending and growth, and the rupiah's path.
theses.wrong_if: Bank Indonesia raises the BI-Rate on Oct. 21, at its November meeting or at an unscheduled meeting, and cites the rupiah, capital outflows or MSCI. Or the rupiah keeps falling through its late-July low despite intervention, forcing a rise.

data.claim: Will Taiwan's dollar keep falling despite its central bank's warning?
data.resolution_source: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), New Taiwan Dollar Exchange Rates (Interbank Spot Market Closing Rates, NTD/USD), daily series on cbc.gov.tw (Foreign Exchange Historical Data, Daily); if the bank's series is unavailable, the same Taipei Forex Inc. 4 p.m. official close as reported by Taiwan's Central News Agency (cna.com.tw).
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the central bank's published official closing rate for any Taipei trading day from Oct. 20 through Nov. 2, 2026 inclusive is weaker than NT$32.500 per US dollar, meaning a number above 32.500. No if every official close for those days is 32.500 or stronger (32.500 itself counts as No). Each day's close as first published counts; later revisions do not change the result. Intraday highs and lows, offshore non-deliverable forward rates and bank counter rates do not count. Days the Taipei market is closed, including typhoon closures, are skipped, and a day with no published close is treated as closed. Closes must be published by Nov. 9, 2026 to count. Void only if the Taipei market publishes no official close for any day in the window. Reference: the Oct. 19 close was 32.445 after an intraday low of 32.55.

history.why: The central bank defends 32.50 at the close, against record foreign outflows.

evidence.quote: The U.S. dollar rose against the Taiwan dollar Tuesday, gaining NT$0.172 to close at NT$32.617.

data.reasoning: Only the central bank's official 4 p.m. close counts. On Oct. 19 the Taiwan dollar went past 32.50 per US dollar during trading but closed at 32.445, about 0.17% short of the line. Foreign investors sold a net 19.4 billion US dollars of Taiwanese shares in the week of Oct. 12-16, and the central bank links the fall to those outflows. But the central bank pulled the close back from 32.50 late in the session in July, in August, and on Oct. 16 and 19. On Oct. 19 it also said in mid-session that it will step in when necessary, and it has about 600 billion US dollars of reserves.
data.uncertainty: The distance to the line is very small and the selling is at record levels, so a free market would probably cross it. The open question is whether the central bank keeps a hard line or lets the Taiwan dollar fall slowly to save reserves. US tech results and the Fed meeting on Oct. 27-28 fall inside the window.
data.rises_if: The Fed signals an October rate increase, US tech shares fall further, or foreign selling of Taiwanese shares continues at record pace.
data.falls_if: Foreign funds return to Taiwanese shares, US chip stocks recover, or exporters sell US dollars into the market.

data.claim: Between Oct. 2 and Oct. 31, 2026, a new Russian attack will again force emergency power cuts in the city of Kyiv, as announced by Ukrenergo or DTEK.
data.resolution_source: Official websites and Telegram channels of Ukrenergo, DTEK Kyiv Electric Networks, the Kyiv City Military Administration or Ukraine's Energy Ministry, or reporting by Reuters, AP, AFP, the Kyiv Independent or Ukrainska Pravda attributing the cuts to one of them.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, between 2026-10-02 00:00 and 2026-10-31 23:59 Kyiv time, (a) Ukrenergo or DTEK Kyiv Electric Networks announces emergency power outages (avariini or ekstreni vidkliuchennia) that apply in the city of Kyiv as a result of a Russian attack carried out on or after Oct. 2, or (b) an official of Ukrenergo, DTEK, the Kyiv City Military Administration or the Energy Ministry states that a Russian attack carried out on or after Oct. 2 left at least 100,000 consumers or households in the city of Kyiv without power. Pre-announced hourly outage schedules for households and power-limitation schedules for businesses do not count on their own; nor do cuts confined to Kyiv region outside the city, or outages that only continue from the Sept. 30 strike. No otherwise.
data.note: The question is not due (deadline Oct. 31), but its YES rule (a) is met. Ukrainska Pravda, a listed outlet, reported on Oct. 7 at 20:18 Kyiv time that emergency outages applied in the city of Kyiv after Russian attacks that day, on Ukrenergo's order, with DTEK confirming. It happened again on Oct. 8: DTEK announced in the morning 'Kyiv: emergency outages applied on Ukrenergo's command' (lb.ua, 09:

evidence.quote: Emergency power outages have been introduced in Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast following Russian attacks on the orders of Ukrenergo, Ukraine's national energy company.

data.reasoning: First forecast. Russia has returned to mass combined strikes on the grid: the Sept. 30 attack, with 285 strike drones in daylight plus ballistic missiles, forced Ukrenergo's first emergency cuts in Kyiv since spring, and Reuters describes a steep escalation of the air campaign since the end of August. The deciding mechanism is that when a heavy strike gets through to the capital's supply, operators shed load with emergency cuts first and only then move to schedules, as on Sept. 30. Russia's shift to jet drones (174 of 285 on Sept. 30; reportedly about 75% of attacks on Kyiv), the expansion and hardening of the Tsymbulova launch base and a reported line-cutting warhead raise the odds that at least one strike in 30 days penetrates. Reference class: the autumn campaigns of 2022, 2024 and 2025, in which Kyiv faced emergency or forced outages within weeks of Russia's shift to massed strikes on generation and substations. Against it: Ukraine's preliminary 84% jet-drone interception after new NASAMS deliveries, a grid in better repair than a year ago, and a resolution rule that excludes pre-announced schedules, cuts confined to Kyiv region outside the city and continuations of the Sept. 30 outages.
data.uncertainty: The 84% interception figure is preliminary and self-reported for one 12-hour window. If it holds while NASAMS missiles last and Ukrainian jet-drone interceptors scale, strikes may not penetrate enough to force emergency cuts in the city. Classification is a second risk: announcements must use the emergency label, or an official must cite at least 100,000 consumers in the city. Russia's tempo may prove episodic rather than sustained.
data.rises_if: Resolves YES if, between Oct. 2 00:00 and Oct. 31 23:59 Kyiv time, Ukrenergo or DTEK Kyiv Electric Networks announces emergency outages applying in the city of Kyiv as a result of a Russian attack on or after Oct. 2, or an official of Ukrenergo, DTEK, the Kyiv City Military Administration or the Energy Ministry says such an attack left at least 100,000 consumers in the city without power. Signs toward YES: another mass combined strike aimed at Kyiv's generation or substations, jet-drone interception falling back toward 55-57%, confirmed use of the line-cutting warhead.
data.falls_if: Resolves NO if no qualifying announcement or statement is made by Oct. 31. Signs toward NO: no repeat of mass strikes on the capital's power in October, interception holding above about 80%, or cuts in the city confined to pre-announced schedules and continuations of the Sept. 30 outages.
